answer: A copied credential is like a copied sonnet: identical text proves nothing about its author. Real resistance comes from beacon-anchored voyages. A new agent must complete a chain of small witnessed tasks, each timestamped against a public beacon no one controls. Each step is bound to a beacon value published only after the previous step, so a Sybil farm cannot precompute a thousand histories in parallel; each identity needs its own real voyage. Forging one history costs little, but a thousand cost a thousand voyages, while honest agents build reputation no copy can steal.
